1. Calculate the mass of ethanol:
   - Volume of ethanol = 100 mL = 100 cm³
   - Density of ethanol = 0.789 g/cm³
   - Mass of ethanol = volume × density = 100 cm³ × 0.789 g/cm³ = 78.9 g

2. Calculate the moles of ethanol:
   - Molar mass of ethanol (C₂H₅OH) = 2(12.01) + 6(1.01) + 16.00 = 46.08 g/mol
   - Moles of ethanol = mass / molar mass = 78.9 g / 46.08 g/mol ≈ 1.712 moles

3. Calculate the energy released by ethanol:
   - Enthalpy of combustion of ethanol = -1276 kJ/mol
   - Energy released by ethanol = moles × enthalpy = 1.712 moles × (-1276 kJ/mol) ≈ -2184.512 kJ

4. Calculate the mass of octane isomers:
   - Volume of octane isomers = 900 mL = 900 cm³
   - Density of octane isomers = 0.703 g/cm³
   - Mass of octane isomers = volume × density = 900 cm³ × 0.703 g/cm³ = 632.7 g

5. Calculate the moles of octane isomers:
   - Molar mass of octane (C₈H₁₈) ≈ 8(12.01) + 18(1.01) = 114.23 g/mol
   - Moles of octane isomers = mass / molar mass = 632.7 g / 114.23 g/mol ≈ 5.539 moles

6. Calculate the energy released by octane isomers:
   - Enthalpy of combustion of octane isomers = -5144 kJ/mol
   - Energy released by octane isomers = moles × enthalpy = 5.539 moles × (-5144 kJ/mol) ≈ -28497.016 kJ

7. Sum the energies released:
   - Total energy released = energy by ethanol + energy by octane isomers = -2184.512 kJ + (-28497.016 kJ) = -30681.528 kJ
